    Reference model

    Layout model

    How curves, reusable types and positioned objects form a layout.

    Entities and relationships

    Reference curves
    Named spatial paths with a color, a starting frame and ordered [length, angle, roll] segments. Length is in metres; angle and roll use radians in JSON and degrees in the editor.
    Types
    Reusable definitions containing a box or cylinder, centerline curvature and roll, magnetic center and length, plus named local frames. Every instance also has implicit center, magnetic_center, magnetic_entry and magnetic_exit frames.
    Objects
    Instances of a type. A position places one target frame on the instance at a transformed world, curve, or object-frame reference.

    Ordered transformations

    Operations are stored as ordered [name, value] pairs and act on the current local x, y and s axes. tx and ty translate transversely; tt translates straight along the current tangent. rx, ry and rs rotate about the current axes.

    ts is a path coordinate. With a curve reference, all ts values are summed to select a curve frame before the remaining operations are applied. In a type-local frame, ts follows the type's curved centerline. tt never follows a curve.

    Inferring a curve station

    A world or object-frame reference can be paired with reference_curve. When its transformation contains ts, the referenced origin P is mapped to a curve station satisfying (P − r(s)) · t(s) = 0. If several stations satisfy the plane equation, the closest curve-frame origin is selected; an error is reported only when there is no solution or the closest solution is ambiguous.

    Viewer interaction

    Use Orbit, Pan and Select in the spatial view. Selecting an entity synchronizes the editors, dependency tree and world-pose panel. The dependency tree starts collapsed at World and follows the actual reference hierarchy.
    Destructive action

    Clear the layout?

    This removes every reference curve, type and object from the editor. Download the current layout first to keep it.
